A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Conformal Policy Control, with complete main text and appendices A–F. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on synthetic losses, medical question answering, constrained active learning, and Ehrlich sequence optimization, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including medical FDR and recall, active-learning risk and MSE, and sequence-optimization outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the constrained-density calculation from min(rho_i, beta)/psi_beta to min(pi_t(A_i), beta*pi_0(A_i))/psi_beta. This limited pseudocode correction aligns the calculation with Eq. (5) and Appendix C.1 already present in v1; it does not establish a new CPC variant or changed experimental implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic non-monotonic losses, MedLFQA, Robot Arm Kinematics, Airfoil, MEPS, and Ehr(32,32)-4-4-4 sequence optimization. The appendix scoring scenarios and risk-level evaluations are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: standard CRC on synthetic losses; monotonized-losses CRC and LTT on medical QA; uncontrolled acquisition and the Lekeufack et al. conformal controller in active learning; and uncontrolled sequence optimization.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices D–F retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, acquisition settings, and Pythia 14M SFT/DPO configuration. Tables 2–5 contain unchanged experimental settings.

E4.justification: The comparison of three medical subclaim-scoring methods in Figure 8 and the additional sequence-optimization risk levels in Figure 9 are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Uncertainty and repeated-run reporting are unchanged. Both versions retain the 25-random-split and standard-error descriptions in Figures 4 and 8, alongside the 10-trial descriptions in Appendix D.4.4 and Table 2.

E6.justification: The plotted results match across versions, including supplementary figures. Reported risk, recall, MSE, optimization-score trends, and qualitative findings are retained; relocated plots do not introduce new results.

T1.justification: Definition 4.1 changes both multiset-deletion notation and the use of random Z versus realized z values. The PDFs do not explain whether this changes the stability assumption or merely repairs notation. Theorem statements, risk bounds, counterexample, and Appendix B proofs are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction now attributes medical FDR control specifically to gCRC and policy-control results to CPC, replacing v1's blanket statement that CPC provides guarantees in all three settings without structural assumptions. The central contributions and empirical success claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds practical interpretation of the safe-policy assumption, including using looser risk tolerances when little is known, and explicitly describes policy-weight smoothness as potentially verifiable or enforceable. The limitations concerning marginal guarantees, context shifts, and tractable likelihoods are retained.

D1.justification: The corrected density expression in Algorithm 1 removes an implementation inconsistency with Appendix C.1. Detailed calibration and sampling instructions, experimental hyperparameters, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: No cited works are added or removed. Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same substantive comparisons and novelty positioning, including the distinction from concurrent Angelopoulos (2026); bibliography changes are formatting edits.

P1.justification: The introduction, CRC background, parts of the method exposition, and Discussion are substantially rewritten. The narrative emphasizes selection bias and prescriptive calibration, adds explanatory examples and notation guidance, and expands the concluding explanation while retaining the overall section organization.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves between columns, Figures 4–6 move to later pages, and Figure 3's caption adopts consistent policy notation. These are limited placement and caption changes; figure graphics and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 explains the selection-bias problem and calibration mechanism more clearly, improves attribution of the medical experiment, and corrects Algorithm 1 to match the existing density definition. These provide limited gains in readability and implementation reliability. Experimental evidence and proofs remain unchanged, and the unexplained notation revision in Definition 4.1 prevents crediting a clear theoretical improvement.
